done_when: Every pytest command in .github/workflows/forge-next.yml and the generated forge.yml adds pytest-timeout with --timeout=150 --timeout-method=thread, so a hung test fails by name with its stack in the log before the job cap; nothing else in the workflows changes

findings.body: The timeout is added only to the generated artifact. `forge.toml:5` still supplies a test command without pytest-timeout or either timeout flag, and `src/forge/sync.py:223–226` inserts that command into the workflow. The write path at `src/forge/sync.py:258–265` overwrites the committed file, so the next `forge sync` on a work branch removes this protection and makes the new regression test fail. Update the generation input so the required timeout survives regeneration, while preserving the existing workflow behavior.
findings.title: Not done: Every pytest command in .github/workflows/forge-next.yml and the generated forge.yml adds pytest-timeout with --timeout=150 --time

why: A test sometimes hangs in Windows test group 1 until the 5-minute job cap cancels the job, and a cancelled job keeps no log, so nobody can see which test hangs
